about: OAIY Desktop's control tools as its MCP server lists them (tools/list), captured from a headless oaiy-server built from main (649ccd1): all of them for a project or setup session; the runner session is offered the read tools named in runner.

tools.description: Overview of OAIY in one call: the engines (running, the model chosen per group, GPUs and memory), services, plugins (state, whether setup is needed), modules, ChatGPT sign-in, the Agent's model, the FormLogic link and sync, setup, and agentMayChange (whether the person lets the Agent change OAIY). Call it first.
tools.name: status
tools.title: OAIY at a glance

tools.description: The engine's models per group: the model chosen, the models installed (the names model_set_default takes), and the catalog's entries with size, memory need (vramGb), recommended and installed (the catalog files background removal and upscaling under picture). Give group for one group only.
tools.name: models_list
tools.title: Engine models

tools.description: How the engine's model downloads stand: each with its status, percent done, speed and any error.
tools.name: model_download_status
tools.title: Model downloads

tools.description: Choose the model a group of the engine uses: model is one of the group's installed models from models_list (not a catalog id). The engines refuse a model the group does not have. Restart the language model (engine_restart) for an llm change to take effect now.

model.description: An installed model of that group, by the name models_list shows.

tools.name: model_set_default
tools.title: Choose a model

tools.description: Start downloading a model from the engine's catalog into the engines' own folder (catalogId: a catalog entry's id from models_list); it is added to its group when done, and model_download_status follows it. Downloads are gigabytes: check size and memory need first.
tools.name: model_download
tools.title: Download a model

tools.description: Start the engine's language model (the model chosen for llm). Answers its state; loading takes a while, and status shows when it is ready.
tools.name: engine_start
tools.title: Start the language model

tools.description: Stop the engine's language model, freeing its GPU memory. Calls, texts and flows that need it fail until it starts again.
tools.name: engine_stop
tools.title: Stop the language model

tools.description: Restart the engine's language model, for example to load a model just chosen with model_set_default.
tools.name: engine_restart
tools.title: Restart the language model

tools.description: The AI sources flows and the Agent can use: OAIY's engine, configured providers and local AI services, ChatGPT (signed in or not, and as whom), and the Agent's own model preference.
tools.name: ai_sources_list
tools.title: AI sources

tools.description: Choose what the Agent itself runs on: source engine (the model chosen in Engines) or chatgpt (the person's ChatGPT sign-in; model is optional, Codex's own default when left out). Live phone calls keep their own fast route either way.

model.description: chatgpt only: a model from Codex's catalogue.

tools.name: agent_model_set
tools.title: Choose the Agent's model

tools.description: Start signing OAIY in to ChatGPT (its Codex connector). Answers the address for the person to open and sign in at (with deviceCode, a code for them to type instead); ai_sources_list shows when they have.

deviceCode.description: Use the device-code sign-in (a code to type) instead of a browser redirect.

tools.name: chatgpt_sign_in
tools.title: Sign in to ChatGPT

tools.description: Sign OAIY out of ChatGPT. Flows and an Agent running on ChatGPT stop working until someone signs in again.
tools.name: chatgpt_sign_out
tools.title: Sign out of ChatGPT

tools.description: OAIY's services (local programs such as the voice server and model servers): each with its status (running, stopped, installing, starting, errored), whether it is installed, and its port. Use the ids with the service tools.
tools.name: services_list
tools.title: Services

tools.description: The last lines a service printed, for why an install or a start failed.

id.description: The service's id, as services_list shows it.

tools.name: service_logs
tools.title: A service's log

tools.description: Install a service (download and set up its files). It runs in the background: service_logs shows its progress and services_list when it is installed.

id.description: The service's id, as services_list shows it.

tools.name: service_install
tools.title: Install a service

tools.description: Start an installed service.

id.description: The service's id, as services_list shows it.

tools.name: service_start
tools.title: Start a service

tools.description: Stop a running service.

id.description: The service's id, as services_list shows it.

tools.name: service_stop
tools.title: Stop a service

tools.description: Remove a service's installed files (for a clean reinstall). Its definition stays, so service_install can put it back.

id.description: The service's id, as services_list shows it.

tools.name: service_uninstall
tools.title: Uninstall a service

tools.description: The installed plugins: id, name, version, state (running, stopped, crashed, disabled…), whether it is switched on, whether its setup is needed (setUpBy: record when finished here, checks when its live checks all pass, as the dashboard judges it), and its connectors' commands (for plugin_command).
tools.name: plugins_list
tools.title: Plugins

tools.description: The plugins OAIY knows how to install, each with what it does and needs, whether it is installed, and the folder on this computer it installs from (source; null when the person has to choose the folder). Pass source to plugin_install.
tools.name: plugin_catalog
tools.title: Plugins to install

tools.description: A plugin's settings, read through its own settings command: the values, and the fields its setup declares (key, label, type, options). Secret-looking values are hidden.

pluginId.description: The plugin's id, as plugins_list shows it.

tools.name: plugin_settings_get
tools.title: A plugin's settings

tools.description: A plugin's setup steps with their live state: recorded done or skipped, a screen step's done check, a requirements step's services and engine models, and whether a step applies; needsSetup as the dashboard judges it, and outstanding lists what is left. Steps of kind permissions, screen and host are the person's to do on screen (plugin_setup_open).

pluginId.description: The plugin's id, as plugins_list shows it.

tools.name: plugin_setup_status
tools.title: A plugin's setup

tools.description: Install (or update) a plugin from a folder or .tar.gz on this computer (source: a path, as plugin_catalog gives it; never a URL). A plugin is native code: install only what the person asked for. Then plugin_enable starts it and plugin_setup_status shows its setup.

source.description: A folder or .tar.gz path on this computer.

tools.name: plugin_install
tools.title: Install a plugin

tools.description: Switch a plugin on and start it. Answers an error, saying why, when it does not start.

id.description: The plugin's id, as plugins_list shows it.

tools.name: plugin_enable
tools.title: Switch a plugin on

tools.description: Switch a plugin off: it stops, and its commands, modules (such as the phone and the calendar) and events are gone until plugin_enable.

id.description: The plugin's id, as plugins_list shows it.

tools.name: plugin_disable
tools.title: Switch a plugin off

tools.description: Stop and start a plugin, for settings that apply only when it starts (plugin_settings_set says when).

id.description: The plugin's id, as plugins_list shows it.

tools.name: plugin_restart
tools.title: Restart a plugin

tools.description: Remove a plugin from this computer, with its data (for the phone plugin, its pairing with the phone).

id.description: The plugin's id, as plugins_list shows it.

tools.name: plugin_uninstall
tools.title: Uninstall a plugin

tools.description: Change some of a plugin's settings through its own settings command: settings holds only the keys to change ({key: value}); plugin_settings_get shows the keys and allowed values, and a value it showed as [redacted] is left as it is. Answers whether they apply only after plugin_restart.

pluginId.description: The plugin's id, as plugins_list shows it.

settings.description: The settings to change, by key.

tools.name: plugin_settings_set
tools.title: Change a plugin's settings

tools.description: Send one of a plugin's declared connector commands (plugins_list lists them), with an optional payload, through the same gate as the dashboard, and answer what it said (secret-looking values hidden). Commands with effects in the world (a call, a text) really happen.

command.description: A command the plugin declares, e.g. phone.status.

payload.description: The command's payload, when it takes one.

pluginId.description: The plugin's id, as plugins_list shows it.

tools.name: plugin_command
tools.title: Send a plugin a command

tools.description: Show the person a plugin's setup in the OAIY dashboard, at a step if stepId is given: for what they must do on screen, such as accepting what the plugin may do or pairing a device.

pluginId.description: The plugin's id, as plugins_list shows it.

tools.name: plugin_setup_open
tools.title: Show a plugin's setup

tools.description: Record a plugin's setup step as done (not its permissions step, which the person accepts on screen).

pluginId.description: The plugin's id, as plugins_list shows it.

tools.name: plugin_setup_step_done
tools.title: Record a setup step done

tools.description: Record a plugin's setup as finished once its steps are done, so OAIY stops asking. Refused until the person has accepted what the plugin may do.

pluginId.description: The plugin's id, as plugins_list shows it.

tools.name: plugin_setup_finish
tools.title: Finish a plugin's setup

tools.description: The flows stored on this desktop: id and name.
tools.name: flows_list
tools.title: Flows

tools.description: One flow's document as stored ({name, nodes, edges}). Read one before flow_create or flow_update, to follow its shape.

id.description: The flow's id, as flows_list shows it.

tools.name: flow_get
tools.title: A flow

tools.description: Store a new flow: flow is its document ({name, nodes, edges}, as flow_get shows); id (letters, digits, - and _) is made from its name when left out. Refuses an id that exists: use flow_update for that.

id.description: The id to store it under.

tools.name: flow_create
tools.title: Create a flow

tools.description: Replace a stored flow's document with a new one (the whole document, as flow_get shows it).

id.description: The flow's id, as flows_list shows it.

tools.name: flow_update
tools.title: Change a flow

tools.description: Run a stored flow with an optional input. By default waits for it (up to timeoutSeconds, 60) and answers its status and output; with wait false, answers the run at once.

id.description: The flow's id, as flows_list shows it.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long the run may take (default 60).

tools.name: flow_run
tools.title: Run a flow

tools.description: Delete a stored flow.

id.description: The flow's id, as flows_list shows it.

tools.name: flow_delete
tools.title: Delete a flow

tools.description: The calendar's settings: business (its name), receptionist (the name the receptionist calls itself on calls and texts; empty means Aokie, and receptionistName is the name it goes by either way), hours (seven days, Monday first, each a list of {open, close} like 09:00), services ({id, name, minutes, description, price}), slotMinutes, noticeMinutes, horizonDays, textConfirmations; available says whether a plugin provides the calendar.
tools.name: calendar_settings_get
tools.title: Calendar settings

tools.description: Change the calendar's settings: only the fields given change, in the shapes calendar_settings_get shows (hours: seven days, Monday first). Needs a plugin that provides the calendar.

business.description: The business's name, as the receptionist says it.

horizonDays.description: How far ahead times are offered.

hours.description: Seven days, Monday first, each a list of {open, close} (HH:MM); an empty list is closed.

noticeMinutes.description: How soon from now a time may be offered.

receptionist.description: The name the receptionist calls itself on calls and texts; empty for Aokie's own name (Aokie).

services.description: The services booked: {id, name, minutes, description, price}.

slotMinutes.description: The step between the times offered.

textConfirmations.description: Text the person when their appointment is confirmed.

tools.name: calendar_settings_set
tools.title: Change calendar settings

tools.description: The people who ring and text, by name: each with key (the last nine digits of their number), number, name (one word is a whole name), nameBy (owner: the person named them; agent: the receptionist did; null: no name), the start of the person's notes for the receptionist, and how many facts the receptionist remembered. q finds names, numbers written any way, notes and facts.

q.description: Find by name, number, notes or what was remembered.

tools.name: contacts_list
tools.title: Contacts

tools.description: One contact by their number: name, nameBy, the person's notes for the receptionist (it reads them on every call and text with them), and facts (what the receptionist remembered, each with its index for contact_forget_fact).

number.description: Their phone number, written any way (0491 570 006, +61491570006, or the key contacts_list shows).

tools.name: contact_get
tools.title: A contact

annotations.title: Name a contact or change their notes

tools.description: Set a contact's name or the person's notes for the receptionist, by their number; the contact is made when there is none. A name set here is the person's: the receptionist never renames them. Only what is given changes; an empty name clears it; notes (up to 2000 characters) replace the notes there.

name.description: Their name as the person wants it; one word is fine (Lance).

notes.description: The person's notes for the receptionist, whole: they replace the notes there.

number.description: Their phone number, written any way (0491 570 006, +61491570006, or the key contacts_list shows).

tools.name: contact_set
tools.title: Name a contact or change their notes

tools.description: Forget one thing the receptionist remembered about a contact: index is the fact's place in contact_get's facts, from 0.

number.description: Their phone number, written any way (0491 570 006, +61491570006, or the key contacts_list shows).

tools.name: contact_forget_fact
tools.title: Forget what the receptionist remembered

tools.description: The FormLogic link (linked or not, the account and address) and how the calendar sync with it stands (state, last success, what is pending, any error).
tools.name: link_status
tools.title: FormLogic link

tools.description: Sync the calendar with FormLogic now and answer how it went. Needs the link and a plugin that provides the calendar.
tools.name: link_sync_now
tools.title: Sync with FormLogic now

tools.description: The first-run setup (finished or not, where it is, what was skipped and which plugins were chosen) and each installed plugin's setup (finished version, steps recorded, whether it needs setup).
tools.name: setup_status
tools.title: Setup

tools.description: Record OAIY's first-run setup as finished, so the dashboard stops offering it.
tools.name: setup_finish
tools.title: Finish first-run setup

tools.description: Show the person a page of the OAIY dashboard: overview, agent, flows, calendar, contacts (the people who ring and text; with contact, that person's own), hours (Hours & Services: the business, its opening hours, services and booking rules), engines, services, plugins, runs, models, python, providers, connections, settings, setup, or a plugin's page as plugin:<pluginId>:<navId>.

contact.description: With view contacts: a person's phone number, written any way, to open their contact.

tools.name: ui_open
tools.title: Show a dashboard page

tools.description: The end of a log: source desktop (the default, OAIY's own), service:<id>, plugin:<id>, or engines, llm or media (the engine's); lines default 100.

source.description: desktop, service:<id>, plugin:<id>, engines, llm or media.

tools.name: logs_tail
tools.title: Logs
